title: Introduce invocation-harvest aggregator + alert-entropy governor for noisy-signal suppression
author: Jordan Meyer
release_notes: Added an invocation harvest aggregator service that compacts sampled invocation fragments into token-level rollups, enriched spans and structured logs; introduced an alert-entropy governor to reduce noisy alerting — configurable, off by default for older tenants.
description:
Summary: This PR adds a lightweight invocation-harvest aggregator that consumes sampled invocation fragments (traces + logs) and produces compact token-level cost and latency rollups, plus a configurable alert-entropy governor that dynamically suppresses alerts driven by low-information noisy signals.

Motivation: We continue to see high alert churn from long-tail invocations that exhibit high variance but low actionable signal. Instead of raising the bar on detection thresholds globally, the aggregator+governor give us a per-cohort mechanism to: 1) retain fidelity for high-value invocations, 2) compress sampled telemetry for cheaper retention and query, and 3) dampen alert noise where entropy indicates low SNR.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3245/harvest-aggregator-design
- [x] Unit tests for aggregation and governor logic
- [x] End-to-end integration test in replaybench
- [x] Grafana dashboard JSON + panel/alert updates
- [x] Runbook stub and rollout plan
- [x] Backwards-compatible config (toggle per-tenant)

What changed (high level commits):
- commit 1: add pkg/observability/harvest/aggregator.go + aggregator interface, buffering, and compact rollup encoding.
- commit 2: instrument span enrichment and add span tag mappings so aggregator can join traces <-> log anchors.
- commit 3: add alert-entropy-governor implementation and runtime config (k8s ConfigMap + feature flag).
- commit 4: dashboards/observability-harvest.json: new Grafana panels for harvest rollups, entropic-alerts gauge, and suppression heatmap.
- commit 5: ops/runbooks/harvest-runbook.md and deploy/k8s/observability-collector.yaml.
- commit 6: unit and integration tests, CI infra changes for new service.

Files changed (representative):
- pkg/observability/harvest/aggregator.go (new): core aggregator, compaction windows, shard key logic
- pkg/observability/harvest/encoder.go (new): compact rollup encoding (jsonlines-friendly, gzipped blobs for long-retention)
- pkg/observability/harvest/collector_service.go (new): k8s entrypoint + graceful shutdown hooks
- observability/config/defaults.yaml: new sampling and suppression defaults
- dashboards/observability-harvest.json: Grafana dashboard and panel definitions
- ops/runbooks/harvest-runbook.md: incident playbook and troubleshooting steps
- deploy/k8s/observability-collector.yaml: deployment + RBAC
- pkg/alerting/entropy_governor.go (new): governor logic and debug endpoints
- tests/unit/aggregator_test.go, tests/unit/entropy_governor_test.go
- sdk/python/redwood/telemetry.py (minor): helper to emit harvest markers and sampling hints

Behavioral notes and compatibility:
- Default behavior is off for tenants without the new config flag. Enabling it for a tenant routes sampled fragments into the aggregator which writes rollups to the existing metrics index (metric names with prefix obs.harvest.*).
- The aggregator emits compact rollups at 1m and 5m windows; the 1m rollups are optional (configurable) and used by fast dashboards; 5m is the canonical retention.
- The entropy governor attaches a suppression score to alerts produced by existing alerting rules; rules can opt-in via annotations, and the governor will lower the alerting weight for cohorts with entropy > threshold. This is a smoothing/attenuation strategy, not a hard mute.

Review conversation (highlights, chronological):
- Sofia Alvarez (reviewer): "Nice isolation between collector and encoder. A couple of thoughts on backpressure — what happens if aggregator can't write to metrics index?"
- Jordan Meyer (author): "Added a bounded retry queue + circuit-breaker state. If write pressure persists we emit an observability.alert_event (low priority) and fall back to rolling local disk (configurable path)."
- Priya Nair (reviewer): "The entropy threshold tuning looks plausible, but we need a short RFC on how we compute entropy (per-token vs per-invocation). Also please ensure we don't shift false positives away from customer-facing SLOs."
- Jordan Meyer: "Added doc section in the design doc and unit tests that assert per-invocation entropy is computed over token-latency distributions; added a regression test simulating false-positive attacks and verified no SLO drift in replaybench."
- Ethan Li (reviewer): "Can we add an e2e that exercises suppression on the replaybench with a synthetic noisy cohort?"
- Jordan Meyer: "Added replaybench scenario 'harvest-noisy-cohort' and e2e pipeline job. CI included it as an opt-in slow test."
- Reviewer approval: Sofia (approved), Priya (approved after small doc updates), Ethan (approved).

CI notes:
- Initial run: build passed, unit tests passed, integration flakes: tests/e2e/replaybench/harvest_noisy_cohort timed out on first try.
- Rerun: flaky timing fixed by bumping timeouts in test harness; final CI status: pass.

Migration and rollout plan:
- Stage 1 (canary): deploy aggregator to observability namespace with flag disabled globally; enable for internal tenants only (2 days).
- Stage 2 (pilot): enable for 10 beta customers, monitor suppression effect and false-negative rate against annotated incidents (1 week).
- Stage 3 (gradual): roll out to 50% of tenants with progressive autoscale and alerting calibration.
- Rollback: toggle feature flag off; aggregator drains and flushes pending rollups.

Observability and monitoring:
- New metrics: obs.harvest.rollup.size, obs.harvest.rollup.latency_p50/p95, obs.harvest.write.errors, obs.entropy.suppression_score
- New spans: harvest.collector.receive -> harvest.aggregator.compress -> harvest.encoder.write (all instrumented with trace IDs for correlation)
- Logging: structured log field harvest_id and cohort_id added to sampled logs; debug endpoint /debug/harvest/state exposes in-memory queue lengths.

Runbook highlights (ops/runbooks/harvest-runbook.md):
- Symptoms: sudden increase in obs.harvest.write.errors or suppression_score spike
- Quick fix: toggle feature flag, restart aggregator pods in order
- RCA pointers: check disk pressure, metrics index write latency, and replaybench scenario results

Backwards compatibility:
- No breaking API changes. Metric names are new but the aggregator writes into existing metric store. The governor is additive and disabled unless explicitly enabled.

Security and privacy:
- Aggregator only consumes already-sampled fragments (no new PII surface created). Rollup encoding strips free-form text unless the tenant opts into enhanced retention (logged in config).

Testing:
- Added unit tests for entropy computation, compaction invariants, and governor attenuation math.
- Added replaybench e2e that simulates noisy cohorts at different shapes and verifies alert delta reduction without SLO drift.

Release notes: See release_notes field.

Misc:
- Added a small CLI tool (pkg/observability/harvest/ctl) to inspect and drain local queue for debugging (admin-only).
- Performance: Aggregator optimized for lock-free ring buffers and uses sharded workers; local bench shows ~5k fragments/sec per pod at 50th percentile CPU on c5-standard-4 equivalent.

Merge: Squash-merged into main on 2025-11-18 by Sofia Alvarez.
